result.result: The notes app is built, and all 12 requirements work at 1280px and 375px wide. Unit tests, browser tests and the production build all pass. I haven't committed anything. Run it with `npm run dev` (http://localhost:5203). - **Libraries:** it uses `marked` to render Markdown and `DOMPurify` to sanitize the output, both added with npm. - **Raw HTML:** it is shown as plain text rather than rendered, and the sanitizer is a second layer behind that. - **Layout:** the editor and preview sit side by side from 1024px up. Below that they stack, and on mobile the sidebar and the editor are separate screens with a "← Notes" back button. - **Checkbox limit:** the preview checkbox is matched to the Nth `- [ ]` line in the source, skipping fenced code blocks. A checkbox-looking line inside an indented (non-fenced) code block would throw that count off. I didn't test that case. - **Reload on a fresh load:** the first load starts with a "Welcome" note. ## What I tested and how - **Logic, 13 unit tests (Vitest, `npm test`):** - sort order (pinned first, then newest) - case-insensitive search across titles and contents - match highlighting and snippets - word count - checkbox toggling, including skipping fenced code and out-of-range indexes - saving and loading, including corrupt data and write failure - Markdown rendering, including script tags, ``, `javascript:` links and raw `` all being neutralized - **Browser, 16 tests (Playwright driving real Chrome, `npx playwright test`):** the same 8 scenarios at 1280px and 375px. - **Layout:** side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile, with no horizontal scroll. - **Rendering:** headings, bold, italic, lists, links, code blocks and checkbox lists. Clicking preview checkboxes updates the source both ways. - **Safety:** a `

Both changes are done: the empty note list now says "Nothing here yet. Create your first note.", and the word count sits in a slim bar at the bottom right of the editor. It's no longer in the toolbar.

I left the "No notes match your search." message alone, since that is a different state from an empty list.

**What I checked**
- **Existing tests:** all 13 unit tests still pass, the TypeScript check is clean, and the 16 earlier browser tests pass at 1280px and 375px wide.
- **New browser test at both widths:** it checks that the word count's bounding box is in the editor's bottom-right corner. It also deletes every note and checks that the list reads exactly "Nothing here yet. Create your first note."
- **Screenshots:** I looked at the desktop empty state and the mobile word-count position (46 words at the bottom right, not covered by the stacked preview). The desktop word-count screenshot is saved but I didn't open it, and I didn't view the mobile empty-state one.

The empty-list screenshot also shows the right pane's own text, "No note selected." with a "+ New note" button. I left that as it was.

Tags work: any `#tag` in a note's text becomes a tag, and the sidebar shows each one with its note count. All 29 unit tests and 30 browser tests pass, and TypeScript is clean. I looked at the screenshots for the tag list, the filter and the suggestion popup. The first run passed, so there was nothing to fix.

How it behaves:
- **What counts as a tag:** `#` followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`, including accented letters, and case-insensitive (`#Work` is `#work`). Headings (`# Title`), URL fragments, `a#b` and pure numbers like `#123` are not tags. Anything inside code (inline or fenced) is ignored too, so a code example doesn't create a tag.
- **Filtering:** clicking a tag filters the list and clicking it again clears the filter. It combines with the search box. If you remove the last use of the filtered tag, the filter clears itself.
- **Suggestions:** typing `#` opens a list of existing tags, most-used first, and narrows as you type. Enter, Tab or a click inserts the tag followed by a space. Arrow keys move through the list and Esc dismisses it. A tag you are still typing is never suggested to yourself, and Enter is a normal newline when no suggestion is showing. I put the suggestion list at the bottom-left of the editor rather than under the caret.
- **Renaming:** the ✎ next to a tag opens an inline field, and Enter applies it. It rewrites the tag in every note's text, whole tags only, so `#work` doesn't touch `#workshop` or code. An invalid name shows an error, and Esc cancels. Renaming to a name that already exists merges the two. Renamed notes count as edited and move to the top of the list.

## What I tested and how

- **Unit tests (Vitest, `npm test`), 16 new tests in `src/lib/tags.test.ts`:**
  - tag extraction (case, unicode, headings, URLs, numbers, code)
  - counts and filtering
  - name validation
  - rename (whole tags only, skipping code)
  - detecting `#` before the caret
  - suggestion ranking
  - inserting a suggestion
- **Browser tests (Playwright in real Chrome, `e2e/tags.spec.ts`), 6 scenarios at both 1280px and 375px wide:**
  - the sidebar shows the right tags and counts
  - filter on, off and combined with search
  - suggestions via Enter, click, arrows and Esc
  - renaming in every note, including an invalid name, Esc, surviving a reload, and renaming the tag that is currently filtered
  - the filter clearing itself
  - no horizontal overflow
- **Regression:** the 18 earlier browser tests still pass at both sizes.
